findings.title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, for example a user notified by a mention or a watched category without ever visiting. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or create the record first.

findings.title: GET request mutates state; repeated visits toggle to muted
findings.body: The unsubscribe action changes notification state on a GET. A second visit (refresh, email prefetchers, link scanners) downgrades regular to muted. The Ember client route also fetches the topic JSON on transition. As a result, users can be muted without intent.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: `tu.save!` does not set `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, and does not publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change`. Open clients therefore keep showing the stale state. Auto-tracking via `update_last_read` (which applies when `notifications_reason_id` is null) can also re-raise the level later.

findings.title: Other emails using unsubscribe_link lack unsubscribe_url
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Every other email that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without passing `unsubscribe_url` will render a missing-interpolation error or a broken 'click here' link. The 'this particular topic' text is also wrong outside topic notifications.

findings.title: Message claims notifications stop even when only downgraded
findings.body: When the user was watching or tracking, the server only downgrades them to regular, so they still get notifications for replies and mentions. The page nevertheless says 'You will stop receiving notifications', which is misleading.
